subject: Fastlane connections ops check-in: concurrency & ratecard next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Tran <olivia.tran@finsight.ai>, Marcus Bennett <marcus.bennett@finsight.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Fastlane connections ops check-in: concurrency & ratecard next steps

Thanks again for the conversation today — great to learn more about how Fastlane will be embedded into your charting pipeline. Quick recap + a few asks so we can size a sensible starting configuration and a draft ratecard/quote.

Recap (from our call)
- Primary workload: real-time assistant/autocomplete for traders; short to medium prompts (avg ~60-100 tokens) and some streaming sessions for live transcription of calls.
- Latency targets: 95th pct <= 250–300ms for generation-first-byte; streaming segments must start emitting within 150–200ms where possible.
- Desired concurrency: you mentioned wanting ~700 parallel UI requests during market open peak, with occasional spikes to ~1.8k for 10–20s.
- Persistence: connections will be long-lived from browser clients via a proxy layer (internal), prefer connection pooling + multiplexing over keepalives.

Asks (so we can propose a config + rate limits)
1) Can you confirm traffic shape: sustained RPS, average session duration, and typical tokens-per-minute for streaming sessions? If you can share an hour-of-day distribution that helps.
2) Do you plan to use server-side multiplexing (HTTP/2) from your proxy, or have many independent browser sockets hitting Redwood?
3) Any hard SLAs required beyond the latency targets above? (e.g., per-request error budget, percent of requests that must be streamed).

What we'll propose after receiving the above
- An initial connection-pool recommendation (keep-alive sockets, per-region pool sizes), multiplexing streams per connection, and expected parallel request concurrency per model.
- Suggested sustained RPS + short burst envelope (we typically size a 3–5x burst over sustained for market spikes).
- A draft ratecard and a Dedicated pool recommendation if you want guaranteed throughput during market open.

Attachments: I attached the call notes (Fastlane-discovery-notes.pdf) and will share an internal quick-start config after you confirm traffic shape.

Next step: if you can reply with traffic estimates (Q1), I’ll loop in Jonas for a proposed technical configuration and a draft quote. If easier, we can do a 30-min scoping call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com

From: Olivia Tran <olivia.tran@finsight.ai>

Subject: Re: Fastlane connections ops check-in: concurrency & ratecard next steps

Thanks, Logan — appreciate the succinct recap. A few quick answers below; I put Marcus on to confirm some numbers.

Traffic shape (today / planned ramp)
- Sustained RPS (per region): 60–80 RPS during regular trading hours; market-open (+/- 15m) ramps to ~310 RPS for ~5–10 minutes.
- Concurrency: our front-end proxies maintain long-lived sockets and multiplex many logical sessions; during peak we estimate 650–800 simultaneous active generation requests (we track active UI requests waiting on completion), with short bursts to ~1.6k when multiple traders refresh.
- Avg tokens: generation requests avg 85 tokens; streaming sessions (conference transcriptions) average 350 tokens over 45–120s; tokens/minute during streaming peaks ~5000 tokens/min/session for heavy callers (rare).
- Session length: most generation calls are sub-2s; streaming sessions last from 30s to 10min depending on the call.

Multiplexing and client topology
- We will use an internal proxy tier that performs server-side multiplexing (HTTP/2), so Redwood sees traffic from a set of proxy IPs rather than thousands of browser sockets.

SLA notes
- We need to maintain the 95th latency goal during market open; if Dedicated is required to hit that, we can consider it. Procurement wants a clear starting quote + an uplift for guaranteed capacity.

Procurement timing
- We are targeting a decision within 3 weeks, with procurement/SC review to follow. We’ll need a clear ratecard and a sample canary run plan for validation.

Happy to jump on a scoping call tomorrow afternoon (CT).

—Olivia
Olivia Tran
Head of Platform Engineering, FinSight
olivia.tran@finsight.ai

Hi Olivia / Marcus — thanks for the detail; super helpful. Based on your numbers I sketched a pragmatic starting configuration and a conservative burst envelope you can validate with a canary. High level below; attaching a brief spreadsheet (redwood-connpool-recs.xlsx) with per-model concurrency and estimated GPU counts.

Suggested starting config (production canary)
- Deployment mode: Hosted with an option to move to Dedicated if market-open SLOs are not met.
- Connection model: proxy-based HTTP/2 multiplexing (recommended). Configure per-proxy keep-alive pool ~120 sockets per proxy IP, with up to 32 concurrent HTTP/2 streams per connection (multiplexing). That yields ~3.8k logical stream capacity per proxy IP (120 * 32), which matches your peak shape if you have ~2 proxy IPs.
- Parallel request concurrency: recommend budgeting 512 concurrent generator calls per model shard for the initial run. If you deploy 2 shards per region that gives ~1k parallel capacity.
- Sustained RPS + burst: propose an initial committed sustained RPS of 100 (per region) with a burst envelope to 400 RPS for windows up to 20s. This aligns with your observed ~310 peak and gives headroom for spikes. If you prefer a higher committed tier to lower unit price, we can size that in the quote.
- Streaming behavior: streaming token emission is supported; we recommend configuring 150ms initial-chunk target and a token emission buffer of 200–300ms. For longer streams we use a separate pool optimized for steady token throughput.
- Fallback and graceful degradation: configure a lower-cost variant (quantized model) as an automated fallback for extreme bursts that exceed both Dedicated and Hosted capacity.

Operational notes
- Rate limits: Hosted standard tier enforces per-tenant QPS and connection limits; for your profile we’ll propose explicit per-proxy connection caps and a per-tenant QPS that maps to the committed RPS. Any bursts beyond the envelope will be rate-limited unless you purchase burst credits or deploy Dedicated capacity.
- Monitoring: we’ll provide route-level latency dashboards, token-cost breakdown, and a canary plan with 1–2% of traffic shifted for 30m to validate latency SLAs during market open.

Next steps
1) Logan / Marissa: I'll draft a short config + pricing note based on the sustained/burst numbers.
2) FinSight: confirm number of proxy IPs and whether you want Dedicated quoted up-front.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical scoping session tomorrow afternoon CT to walk the canary plan.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
